Share county counts across smaller Census areas

Source: R/extrapolate_from_county.R
extrapolate_from_county.Rd

extrapolate_from_county() shares each county's count across the county's census tracts or block groups, in proportion to each area's population in the same stratum, from the American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates. Run it on county data that has been through impute_suppressed().

The estimates are modelled, not observed: they assume the same rate in every area of a county within a stratum.

For Knowledge of Status, county_cases is the number of people with HIV who know their status, and it is shared across areas by their residents, as if people with HIV lived in each area in proportion to its population. The ACS columns are residents, not people with HIV, so area_cases / area_population_acs is not the percentage who know their status.

Usage

extrapolate_from_county(
  x,
  to = c("tract", "block group"),
  no_county = c("report", "spread"),
  spread_by = c("population", "cases"),
  empty_strata = c("total", "equal", "none"),
  ages = c("auto", "13+", "all"),
  race_table = c("B03002", "B01001"),
  unknown_race = c("report", "redistribute"),
  unknown_age = c("report", "redistribute"),
  unestimated = c("leave out", "error"),
  missing_population = c("leave out", "error"),
  acs_year = NULL,
  weights = NULL
)

Arguments

x

County data from get_atlas() that has been through impute_suppressed(), with at most one stratification variable.

to

The areas to share county counts across. Both nest inside counties, so the estimates add up to the county counts exactly:

  • "tract" (default): census tracts. ACS 5-year estimates from 2009.

  • "block group": census block groups. ACS 5-year estimates from 2013; smaller areas have larger ACS margins of error.

Areas that cross county lines, such as ZCTAs, are not supported yet.

no_county

Cases in state totals with no county (see no_county_cases()):

  • "report" (default): left out of the estimates, with a message giving the total. The report is kept in attr(result, "no_county_cases").

    For CDC's HIV estimates, whose county data cover only the Ending the HIV Epidemic (EHE) counties, the remainder can include people in counties outside EHE coverage, and a message says so.

  • "spread": shared across the state's counties in x by their ACS population in the same stratum, then across areas as usual. x must hold every county CDC reports in each of its states, for each indicator, year and stratum it has (rows CDC lists as "Data not available" with no count aside), or the counties left out would have their cases spread too; to study part of a state, spread first and filter the result. Checking needs CDC's county table, which comes from the cache when x was downloaded in this session. Negative remainders are not spread, nor are remainders in a state with no allocated county in that stratum; the message says how many cases could not be spread. Not available for CDC's HIV estimates (EHE counties only).

With either choice, a warning (class "cdcatlas_state_unplaced_cases") names any state with more than 25% of its cases in no county row; see no_county_cases(). With "report", county and area estimates for such a state are too low by about that share. With "spread", those cases are placed by assumption, not by data on where they are.

spread_by

How no_county = "spread" shares a state's remainder among its counties:

  • "population" (default): by each county's ACS population in the stratum, as if cases with no county lived anywhere in the state.

  • "cases": in proportion to each county's own count in the stratum, as if cases with no county resembled cases with one. A state stratum with no county cases falls back to population.

Ignored for no_county = "report".

empty_strata

What to do when CDC reports cases in a county stratum but no area in the county has ACS population in it (for example a small county with no residents of one age group):

  • "total" (default): share by the areas' total population.

  • "equal": share equally across the county's areas.

  • "none": leave the estimates NA, with a warning.

ages

Ages the Census populations cover:

  • "auto" (default): 13 and older for HIV indicators (as CDC reports them), all ages otherwise, decided indicator by indicator, so x can combine HIV with other diseases.

  • "13+" or "all": set it yourself.

When x is stratified by age, the age groups set the ages and ages is ignored: HIV groups start at 13, so the total population (the "total" fallback for empty strata) is ages 13 and older; other diseases' groups cover all ages.

race_table

The ACS table for race populations, used when x is stratified by race:

  • "B03002" (default): Hispanic or Latino origin by race. Its groups match AtlasPlus exactly (Hispanic, and non-Hispanic for each race), but it has no ages, so for ages 13 and older each area's populations are scaled by the area's share of residents aged 13 and older.

  • "B01001": the sex-by-age tables for each race (B01001B to B01001I), which give ages 13 and older directly. Only White (B01001H) and Hispanic (B01001I) match AtlasPlus; the other groups include Hispanic people of that race.

unknown_race

Cases CDC reports with race "Unknown", when x is stratified by race:

  • "report" (default): left out, with a message, and listed in attr(result, "not_allocated").

  • "redistribute": shared across the county's known race groups in proportion to their counts, within each indicator and year, then across areas as usual. A county with no cases of known race keeps its unknown cases unallocated.

unknown_age

Cases CDC reports with age "Unknown" (chlamydia, gonorrhea and syphilis), when x is stratified by age:

  • "report" (default): left out, with a message, and listed in attr(result, "not_allocated").

  • "redistribute": shared across the county's known age groups in proportion to their counts, within each indicator and year, then across areas as usual. A county with no cases of known age keeps its unknown cases unallocated.

unestimated

Suppressed rows impute_suppressed() couldn't estimate (cases_source = "not estimated", with no count), such as a county CDC still lists after it was abolished:

  • "leave out" (default): left out, with a message naming the counties, and listed in attr(result, "not_allocated"). Their cases count towards the state's remainder with no county.

  • "error": stop with an error.

missing_population

What to do when the ACS population is missing (an NA estimate, or a variable the Census didn't return) for some area of a county:

  • "leave out" (default): leave that county stratum out, with a warning, and list it in attr(result, "not_allocated") with reason "missing ACS population". Sharing over the other areas would move cases.

  • "error": stop instead.

A population of 0 is not missing; see empty_strata.

acs_year

The last year of the ACS 5-year estimates. NULL (default) uses each data year. A single year can be given only if x has one year.

weights

Not yet supported; reserved for sub-county weights.

Value

A tibble with one row per county, area, indicator, year and stratum (see below for the one tract that is in two counties):

year, acs_year

Data year and ACS year used.

area_type, geoid, area_name

to, and the area's Census GEOID and name.

county_fips, county_name, state_fips

The county and state the area is in.

indicator, race_ethnicity, sex, age, data_status

From x.

county_cases, cases_source, county_population_atlas

The county's count, where it came from (see impute_suppressed()) and CDC's county population.

county_cases_spread

Cases with no county added to this county (no_county = "spread"); 0 otherwise.

county_cases_unknown

Cases of unknown race or age added to this group (unknown_race or unknown_age = "redistribute"); 0 otherwise.

county_cases_allocated

county_cases + county_cases_spread + county_cases_unknown: what the county's areas add up to.

area_population_acs, county_population_acs

ACS population in the stratum, for the area and the sum of the county's areas.

area_total_population, county_total_population

The same for the whole population at the same ages.

allocation

How the county's count was shared: "stratum population", "total population", "equal shares" or "none" (see empty_strata).

area_cases

Estimated cases in the area.

area_population_acs - area_cases means different things by indicator:

  • HIV prevalence (people living with diagnosed HIV): residents aged 13 and older without diagnosed HIV, which includes people with undiagnosed HIV.

  • Estimated HIV prevalence (diagnosed and undiagnosed): closer to residents without HIV, under the estimate's own assumptions.

  • Other indicators: no such meaning. New diagnoses and incidence need the population at risk, which excludes people already living with HIV; chlamydia, gonorrhea and syphilis count infections rather than people; for Knowledge of Status the population isn't residents.

It can be negative where empty_strata shares cases into a stratum with no ACS population.

geoid is unique within county_fips (for one indicator, year and stratum), not overall. With ACS 2010 to 2019, one 2010 tract (09013890201) is split between two of Connecticut's planning regions, so it has two rows with the same geoid, one for each planning region in x, and so does each of its block groups. Each row holds a share of the area: both area_population_acs and area_total_population are multiplied by the share of the tract's land area in that planning region, and area_cases is that county's count shared over them. Block groups inherit their parent tract's land-area shares, which are not measured shares of each block group's population. A warning of class "cdcatlas_duplicated_geoid" says how many areas are affected.

To get one row per area, for example before joining to tract boundaries, sum area_cases, area_population_acs and area_total_population by geoid within year, indicator and stratum; keeping one of the two rows would understate the tract. The county columns repeat on every row of a county and must not be summed. The article "Extrapolation to tracts" shows the step.

Two attributes record what was not allocated: attr(result, "no_county_cases"), the no_county_cases() report, and attr(result, "not_allocated"), county rows left out, with a reason.

Details

The denominator is the sum of the county's areas, so the estimates add up to county_cases_allocated in every county stratum.

Census populations come from ACS tables requested by variable code: B01001 (sex by age) for all ages, sex and age, and for race the table set by race_table. Each CDC age group counts the share of each B01001 age band that its ages cover, assuming ages are spread evenly within a band: for ages 13 and older (and HIV's 13-24 group), 2/5 of the 10 to 14 band. get_atlas() requests each disease's own age groups, which cover its ages once.

County rows with no Census denominator are left out and listed in attr(result, "not_allocated"): race "Other", race or age "Unknown" (unless redistributed), suppressed rows with no estimate (see unestimated), rows kept by impute_suppressed(not_available = "keep"), and counties with no ACS areas (such as Valdez-Cordova, Alaska, which CDC still lists with no population).

CDC reports every year on its current county map. ACS releases from 2006-2010 to 2015-2019 use 2010 tracts, so in Connecticut (now planning regions) and the old Valdez-Cordova Census Area, Alaska (now Chugach and Copper River), each 2010 tract and its block groups are assigned to the current county they fall in. The one 2010 tract split between two planning regions is shared by land area. The crosswalk ships in inst/extdata/tract-2010-crosswalk.csv. It is derived by data-raw/tract-crosswalk.R (in the package's GitHub repository) from two Census Bureau relationship files: the 2020-to-2010 census tract files for Connecticut and Alaska, and the 2022 county subdivision to census tract file for Connecticut, which gives each tract its planning region. These are US government works, in the public domain in the United States.

CDC's current county codes the package knows an ACS release lacks:

  • Connecticut's planning regions: handled by the crosswalk for ACS 2010 to 2019; missing from ACS 2009, 2020 and 2021, which code Connecticut by its old counties; in ACS 2022 on.

  • Chugach and Copper River, Alaska: handled by the crosswalk for ACS 2010 to 2019; missing from ACS 2009; in ACS 2020 on.

  • Kusilvak, Alaska (02158, formerly Wade Hampton 02270) and Oglala Lakota, South Dakota (46102, formerly Shannon 46113), renamed in 2015: missing from ACS releases before 2015.

This list is not a full check of every ACS vintage against CDC's map. Counties a release doesn't match are left out with a warning that says why, for the cases above. In 2010-2019 a block group follows its tract: the block groups of the one split tract (09013890201) are shared between Capitol and Northeastern Connecticut planning regions by the tract's land area, not by where each block group lies.

Tract and block group boundaries change every ten years, so estimates from ACS years on different sides of a decennial census (2017 and 2022, say) can't be compared area by area.

Needs the tidycensus package and a Census API key in the CENSUS_API_KEY environment variable (see tidycensus::census_api_key()). Also downloads the matching state data from CDC AtlasPlus for the no-county report.

Congenital syphilis isn't supported: its rates are per 100,000 live births, so Census populations are the wrong denominator.

See also

impute_suppressed(), no_county_cases(); the article "About CDC AtlasPlus data" on CDC's county map and the Census denominators.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
county <- get_atlas("hiv", "county", 2022, stratify_by = "sex")
county <- impute_suppressed(county)
tracts <- extrapolate_from_county(county)
block_groups <- extrapolate_from_county(county, to = "block group")

# Cases left out because they have no county
attr(tracts, "no_county_cases")
} # }
